description:
Aggregate and browse AI coding agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.) in one place. Desktop app, self-hosted server, or Docker.

Codeg (Code Generation) is an enterprise-grade multi-agent coding workspace. It unifies local AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw, Cline, etc.) in a desktop app, standalone server, or Docker container — enabling remote development from any browser — with conversation aggregation, parallel git worktree development, MCP/Skills management, chat channel interactions (Telegram, Lark, iLink, etc.), and integrated Git/file/terminal workflows.
This release adds conversation moves between folders, clearer tracking of background work, and more convenient repository collaboration, while improving file search, memory usage and agent compatibility.
New
- Move idle conversations that are not tied to a task between open folders, individually or in bulk, with menu selection and folder search while keeping their history.
- Control the desktop Web Service from the status bar, with its current status, start/stop controls and a new option to allow connections only from this computer.
- PR/MR lists show CI status, passing/total counts and approval reminders, with direct access to check details and approval of GitHub workflows awaiting maintainer authorization.
- Agents can attach files and images when creating to-do tasks, keeping reference material alongside the task instructions.
Improved
- Track background tasks and sub-agents from the running count above the chat input, including work that continues after a reply ends and delegated agents awaiting your response.
- Redesigned Session Details and message navigation make it easier to find the running message, inspect sub-agents and review file changes.
- Codex sub-agent activities now appear as expandable timeline steps, with task details, replies, errors and a shortcut to open the child conversation.
- Task completion comments can include an agent-drafted reply that you review and edit before publishing, with an optional Codeg footer.
- File search uses less frontend memory and avoids repeatedly scanning the same workspace, while keeping results current as files change in open projects. (#1116 by @kogekiplay)
- Updated Cursor to 2026.11.11-b912975, Kimi Code to 2.6.0, Qoder to 1.1.87, CodeBuddy to 2.183.0 and the ZCode bridge to 0.84.2.
Fixed
- Further reduced memory retained by very long tool output and closed HTML previews. (#1132, #1137 by @kogekiplay)
- Codex MCP screenshots and image results display correctly in desktop and Web chat, including after reopening a conversation. (#1134 by @PengXiaoyi)
- Kimi MCP authorization correctly shows the browser authorization link and reconnection status while waiting. (#1133 by @Cuinnchen)
- Kimi Code 2.6.0 plan reviews no longer incorrectly appear as tool failures when you approve, dismiss or request changes, both during the conversation and in its history.
- The ZCode bridge supports encrypted credentials used by ZCode 3.18+, fixing related execution failures and improving handling of duplicate history messages and replies.
- Interactive question cards for agents such as DeepSeek Harness correctly display the question text and option descriptions, fixing cases where only a short label appeared. (#1140 by @mvanhorn)
- Antigravity instances configured as custom agents correctly display interactive questions and preserve your selections in conversation history. (#1127 by @ana52070)
- Questions that only accept preset choices, including applicable Antigravity and Pi questions, no longer offer an unsupported “Other” input, preventing typed answers from being treated as cancellations. (#1131 by @ana52070)
- Custom Antigravity instances on Windows now include their startup temporary files in automatic cleanup, reducing disk space buildup after repeated launches. (#1139 by @ana52070)
- Long content in dialogs such as the model picker no longer causes horizontal overflow or clips buttons.
- Fixed an occasional cleanup error when an agent connection ends.
Thanks to @kogekiplay, @ana52070, @PengXiaoyi, @Cuinnchen and @mvanhorn for contributing to this release.
